inspection: Each of the five full original PNGs was actually opened separately with view_image, original detail, before planning. No source page or passed science gate repeated.

A vertical dashed guide joins K to a temperature-axis mark with a critical-temperature subscript that reads Cyrillic k. No horizontal pressure guide or critical-pressure value.
figures.modern_mapping: Preserve the endpoint and nonzero schematic curve start; use Latin subscript k in the critical-temperature label. Canvas coordinates describe shape, not measured data or a fitted saturation law.

observed: One p-up/T-right axis frame with arrowheads and 0 at the origin; no numerical ticks.
Increasing convex low-temperature curve changes to a straight rising continuation at the evaporation endpoint; the curve and line meet continuously.
A vertical dashed line from the change point reaches T with a small subscript visually reading 1. There is no K label or filled critical-point marker.
figures.modern_mapping: Preserve T1 and the two-piece continuous path. Regularize the continuation to the fixed-mass/fixed-volume ideal-gas proportionality in the frozen prose, without drawing a new extrapolation ray to the origin or claiming calibrated slopes. This path requires evaporation before the critical point and the subsequent dilute-gas approximation.
uncertainties: The tiny source breakpoint subscript is treated as the visually apparent 1, not a measured temperature or a critical-temperature identity.

Upper liquid-density branch decreases; lower vapor-density branch increases. They join at the same right-hand critical endpoint, with steep terminal tangents.
A vertical dashed guide descends from that shared endpoint to a critical-temperature label. Source Chinese labels identify liquid above and vapor below; no K marker, density values or extra branches.
figures.modern_mapping: Translate the branch names to Liquid/Vapor and the critical subscript to Latin k. Preserve a single shared frame, branch order and equality at the endpoint. The sketch has no physical scale; the left axis attachment does not assert actual material data at absolute zero.

observed: One thick-walled rounded-bottom vessel in section, closed by a heavy flat lid/flange. Left/right bolted clamps retain the lid.
Liquid occupies the lower large part with horizontal texture and an upper surface; vapor headspace remains between the water and lid. No heater or bubble population.
A horizontal external lever with a left fitting and a right pivot is above the lid; a central descending stem intersects the lid. Exact internal valve action is not labeled.
An upper-right circular gauge is connected to a lid port by a bent tube. The small face marks are not readable calibration data.
figures.modern_mapping: Deterministically show the vessel, sealed lid, two fasteners, lever/stem, bent pressure connection and uncalibrated pointer gauge. Water/Steam/Gauge are modern English identifications, not copied source labels. No medical result, pressure setting, sterilization timing or operation instruction.
uncertainties: Do not assign numerical values to the unreadable gauge face.
Do not invent a specific operating mechanism for the small top fittings beyond their visible structure.

observed: One arched bell jar, top lifting loop and sealed baseplate, surrounding an open beaker on the left and a support stand on the right.
The beaker has a liquid surface below its rim and multiple hollow bubble marks below that surface.
A long thermometer-like instrument passes through a horizontal clamp into the beaker; its lower sensing part is submerged. The clamp joins the right-hand stand.
A base outlet descends below the plate, bends right and ends in a rightward arrow toward the pump. No heater, numerical temperature or pressure scale.
figures.modern_mapping: Keep the jar/beaker containment, immersed thermometer, stand/clamp and rightward pump connection. English Bell jar/Thermometer/Water/To pump are identification additions. Bubble locations/count are illustrative, not a measurement or a claim that every liquid point nucleates at once. No child operation or exact pressure/temperature setting.
uncertainties: The instrument's small interior markings are not a readable scale and will not be supplied with invented values.
